title: Industry practice in term incorporation
summary: Evidence of customary allocation can affect whether an added term objectively surprises a merchant.
notes: Bayway uses trader testimony and sample contracts rather than the buyer’s personal reaction alone. A form bundling tax into the price can reflect the same allocation as one separately billing it; a silent form does not necessarily contradict an otherwise established practice. The party capable of avoiding the tax supplies part of the court’s reasoning. This is the assigned application, not the complete later course unit on usage of trade and course of dealing.

sources.label: Farnsworth et al., Contracts: Cases and Materials, 10th ed. (2023), pp. 285–289. Open assigned page 285.
